moat_against: Commodity cover re-shopped at renewal; low policyholder switching costs and non-exclusive intermediated distribution
No structural pricing power: renewal rate flat in Q2 2026 as the pricing cycle softens
Larger rivals (Chubb, Travelers, AIG) set competitive terms in commercial lines
Social inflation pressuring loss ratios; underlying combined ratio deteriorated to 94.2% in Q2 2026
Recurring legacy mass-tort/asbestos charges in Corporate & Other ($77M after-tax in Q2 2026, $88M in Q2 2025) and LTC runoff drag
Catastrophe tail and controlled-company structure with a thin public float
moat_for: Scale: seventh-largest U.S. commercial insurer with Specialty / Commercial / International breadth
AM Best A+ financial strength rating (upgraded December 2025) supporting broker and policyholder trust
Specialty underwriting expertise in professional liability, surety (Western Surety) and healthcare lines
Expense ratio held below 30% (29.7% FY2025) while investing in technology/AI
Retention 83% with new business +11% to a record $718M in Q2 2026
Loews' ~92% ownership as a historically supportive long-horizon parent
moat_justification: Weak-to-narrow moat: a scaled, A+-rated specialty/commercial franchise (seventh-largest U.S. commercial insurer; Specialty/Commercial/International breadth; expense ratio held below 30%; retention 83% with record new business) — but P&C cover is re-bid at renewal through non-exclusive brokers/agents, pricing power belongs to the industry cycle (renewal rate flat in Q2 2026), far larger rivals (Chubb, Travelers, AIG) set competitive terms, and measured returns sit at the cost of capital through the cycle (ROE 5.43%/10.66%/7.98%/12.18%/9.12%/11.00% across 2020-2025 in fundamentals.json; FY2025 combined ratio 94.7%, underlying 91.8%, deteriorating to 94.2% underlying in Q2 2026), with recurring legacy mass-tort charges and LTC runoff as persistent drags and Loews' ~92% control leaving minority holders no governance say.
name: CNA Financial Corporation
one_liner: Mid-tier commercial P&C insurer with an A+ rating and disciplined underwriting, moat 4/10 — engine prints Tier A (weighted IRR 21.95%, IV@15% $75.11 vs $47.90) on an OCF base that capitalizes insurer float, so the final tier is softened to B at low confidence; it clears 15% at ~$75 on engine numbers, with the bear-case cushion (~$52) the honest margin of safety.
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH insurer artifact: the OCF-based OE base capitalizes float/reserve growth (NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE is structural in 2023, 2024 and 2025 — FY2025 OCF $2,490,000,000 vs net income $1,278,000,000, and maintenance OE $1,278,000,000 vs conservative OE $2,363,000,000), so tier-by-numbers A overstates distributable owner's earnings; softened one notch to B, confidence low — the standing insurer-float treatment, same as PFG/HIG.
